In addition to encouraging staff to undertake sustainability-related courses and obtain relevant qualifications, the HKMA has gained relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process of engaging external consultants since 2021 to advise on leading industry practices for portfolio climate transition. The HKMA also uses ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to supplement its ongoing portfolio analysis, helping strengthen the Exchange Fund’s ESG resilience.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its own carbon footprint, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier and contributing to Hong Kong’s overall climate goals. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to caring for employees’ physical and mental well-being, promoting financial inclusion and discharging its social responsibilities. The HKMA is committed to conducting its day-to-day operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts sustainability principles into practice under three pillars: the environment, employees and social responsibility (Figure 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the formulation and implementation of the HKMA’s sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk and Compliance Department and the Corporate Development and Services Department, and submits regular reports to the Governance Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the Committee’s leadership, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing initiatives in their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved climate targets for corporate operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review progress on the HKMA’s green initiatives, including recommendations for enhancing the HKMA’s sustainable procurement policies, procedures and practices. Sustainability Governance Structure The HKMA’s Corporate Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA attaches great importance to its own carbon footprint and has established internal Green Office Guidelines to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. Environmental considerations have been incorporated into the interior design, operation, repair and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA a Gold rating for certain renovated office areas. This was the HKMA’s second green building certification, following the LEED Gold certification received in 2021. Awarded a Gold rating under BEAM Plus Interiors Version 1.0 The HKMA implemented a number of energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption6 in 2022 was 4,996.4 megawatt-hours, or 2.8 megawatt-hours per person7, representing a decrease of 24.4% from 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions8 in 2022 were 2,996.4 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e), or 1.7 tCO2e per person, representing a decrease of 38.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emissions Intensity (Scopes 1 and 2) The HKMA promotes paperless internal operations. It has also implemented a print management system under which employees must log in to a printer to confirm each print request, helping reduce unnecessary printouts and toner consumption. Where printing is necessary, double-sided and black-and-white printing is encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic record-keeping system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 metric tonnes, or 0.0114 metric tonnes per person, representing a decrease of 65.3% from 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Consumption Intensity The HKMA’s waste management efforts continue to follow the “4R” principle. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit analysing the composition of waste generated by its offices. The audit found that food waste accounted for a significant proportion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see “Enhancing Waste Management” on page 41). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022, including general and recyclable waste, was 242.0 metric tonnes, or 0.135 metric tonnes per person, representing a decrease of 4.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuations in the trend were mainly attributable to work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Figure 3 Non-hazardous Waste Intensity The HKMA gives top priority to waste reduction at source and is committed to reducing, reusing and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste generated in its daily operations, including plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood and electronic products, and to provide waste-reduction recommendations. Based on the audit findings, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, installing food waste collection bins in all pantries. Food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for electricity generation. Residues from the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. Recycling bins are also conveniently located throughout the offices. The HKMA shares recycling tips with employees and places greater emphasis on further improving the sorting of recyclables at source, as well as precautions for handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers and beverage bottles. In addition, we continue to organise activities to raise employees’ environmental awareness, explain waste management policies and encourage employees to make good use of recycling facilities in the offices. Daily food waste collections transported to an organic resources recovery centre Recycling plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres, one for operations and the other for backup. As they account for a major share of the organisation’s overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and a range of energy-saving measures, including in-row air-conditioning systems, light-emitting diode lighting and round-the-clock monitoring of electricity consumption efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations for improving overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also begun to obtain green data centre certification. Recognising the importance of building a sustainability culture, the HKMA regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage employees to develop sustainable habits and adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips and annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics with employees, reminding them to help address environmental issues at the individual level. Employees are also encouraged to make suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager in the Administration Division, a focus group brings together employees from different departments to brainstorm ideas and specific measures for promoting a green working environment. Focus group members also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly working practices and has introduced various measures to improve the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry and the economy as a whole, while minimising resource consumption. The HKMA’s Submission Through Electronic Transmission system (STET) is a one-stop platform that enables banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various regular returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly or annual basis. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel through which the HKMA issues information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. The two systems save a substantial amount of paper each year. In handling banking complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has adopted measures to support paperless document submission, enabling bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a next-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper consumption, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account-opening and account-termination letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore additional green initiatives, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities, the HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payment methods instead of cash and physical cheques. Further information on FPS and stored value facilities is provided in the chapter “Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre” in the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic red packets is simple and convenient, and reduces the use of physical red packets and banknotes, thereby contributing to Hong Kong’s sustainable development. To this end, the HKMA continued to promote electronic red packets actively across social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute them during the Lunar New Year through online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various campaigns to attract users to electronic red packets, such as providing festive user interfaces, enhancing functionality for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cash-rebate promotions. The HKMA promotes electronic red packets on social media For members of the public who choose to distribute physical red packets during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of “good-as-new notes”, namely used but still crisp banknotes, in red packets. Good-as-new notes reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening environmental impacts. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that good-as-new notes have gained increasing public acceptance in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA’s efforts to promote coin recycling. Coins collected under the Programme are recirculated to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The Programme operates two Coin Carts and has so far served more than one million customers, collecting over 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HKD1.3 billion. In 2022, around 78% of users chose to deposit part or all of the value of their coins into stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service by deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on flag days organised by non-governmental organisations, in support of social services. Coin-counting machine on a Coin Cart Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme is the world’s first systematic coin collection programme to adopt a mobile vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received a number of local and international awards in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The Programme operates two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, deposit the value into stored value facility accounts such as Octopus cards or e-wallets, or donate it to The Community Chest. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are occasionally deployed for various educational activities, such as student visits.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) climate targets (“Climate Targets”). The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (“SBTi Corporate Manual”). The purpose of this verification was to verify whether the Climate Targets had been developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shum Siu-yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023 Verification Statement The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2022 environmental data (“2022 Data”). The 2022 Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as changes in these data compared with 2015 levels. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute (“WRI”) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (“WBCSD”). The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The verification scope comprised a total of six office and warehouse properties: four offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and two warehouses at 5) Lok Sing Industrial Centre and 6) Chong Li Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six properties. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the data were tested by tracing selected sample data to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency’s verification team was not involved in preparing the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu-yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. Almost half of this critical decade for addressing the climate crisis has already passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% during this decade to have any hope of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window of opportunity for limiting the rise in global temperature to within 1.5 degrees Celsius is rapidly closing. The impact of a 1.1-degree Celsius rise in temperature is already clearly being felt by everyone—extreme weather events such as record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms are occurring frequently around the world, with each event more serious than the last. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, shortly after being battered by a powerful super typhoon, we experienced a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our sound infrastructure and ability to respond swiftly to disasters, the impact was still extremely serious—widespread flooding, traffic disruption and damage to roads in many locations. All these events clearly remind us that there is no time to lose in taking decisive and ambitious climate action. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on its path towards a low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that properly balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means easy. Owing to the region’s rapid economic development and population growth, it accounts for more than half of global carbon emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is highly populated and, because of its geographical location, is also vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather. As regional economies are at different stages of development, the low-carbon transition will create new opportunities for some economies, but raising the capital required for the transition will be a tremendous challenge for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capacity and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As the banking sector regulator, a market facilitator and a responsible investor, the HKMA has devoted substantial efforts to the sustainability agenda. The chapters of this report describe the specific measures and initiatives introduced by the HKMA over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA’s internal governance structure and coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas more effectively, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For details of the Steering Committee, please refer to the new chapter entitled “Sustainability Governance”. Hong Kong banks play an important role in supporting Asia’s transition to net zero. In addition to performing our traditional role as the banking sector regulator by ensuring through our day-to-day supervisory work that banks properly manage climate risk, we also act as a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in providing finance for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype green taxonomy framework for consultation in May and are now refining the framework in light of the feedback received during the consultation. In addition, as demand grows for higher-quality sustainability disclosures that are more comparable globally, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued in June by the International Sustainability Standards Board, which constitute a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting. The HKMA’s role as a facilitator extends beyond establishing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing the pain points faced by the industry. Many banks currently find it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments because of data limitations. In view of this, the HKMA will soon launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. By simply entering a property address, banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping them manage the associated climate risk. As a leading international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects in Asia and supporting the region’s low-carbon transition. In recent years, international green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong have accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, placing Hong Kong well ahead of other centres. Particularly noteworthy is that the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive years respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong’s important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The vibrant development of Hong Kong’s sustainable bond market is attributable in part to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$25 billion in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to innovate and broaden the features of green bonds, including their currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world’s largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world’s first tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second tokenised green bond offering. Denominated in four major currencies and issued in digitally native form, it was the world’s first multi-currency digital green bond issuance. At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the dynamism and competitiveness of Hong Kong’s sustainable finance ecosystem. These cover a range of areas, including skills training, data enhancement, green fintech and transition finance. In talent development in particular, we introduced a new “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in 2023, providing banking practitioners with a structured curriculum to deepen their understanding and professional knowledge of green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work. It provides capital for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing those sectors from being unable to transition owing to a lack of funding support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong’s green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also broaden the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, thereby encouraging regional corporates to raise transition capital in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen engagement with relevant stakeholders and use public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private-sector investment in sustainable development projects that have traditionally found it more difficult to obtain finance. Some of the above work requires cross-sector collaboration and is coordinated mainly by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our longstanding collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also became a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership in 2023. The Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to establish a Hong Kong chapter. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of capital into sustainable development projects across the region and around the world. To promote new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year. It attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including leading decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, who discussed ways to scale up climate finance in the region and forged new partnerships for this purpose. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivers remarks at the Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum, a flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week. As the manager of Hong Kong’s official reserves and a significant global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of investment in green and sustainable assets and has progressively expanded the Exchange Fund’s ESG and green asset portfolios in the public and private markets. In support of the target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s Investment Portfolio by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while extending the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA for investment outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the proposition of “doing well by doing good”. In the private markets, we continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio had fallen by 6% and 46% compared with its 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and remained below the overall market level. As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement by formulating our sustainability goals and plans around the three pillars of the environment, our people and social responsibility. Specifically, on our low-carbon transition journey, the HKMA continuously strengthens its capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency enhancement and waste management, with the ultimate aim of fulfilling our commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have developed plans to eliminate Scope 1 emissions entirely in the near term and have made good progress towards our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to perform the HKMA’s various important functions, the HKMA is committed not only to its green objectives but also to promoting the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In addition, through collaboration with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing the public’s financial literacy and raising public awareness of financial fraud prevention. The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. As economies around the world move towards a more sustainable future, the process is expected to bring profound changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transition carries considerable risks, but it will also bring unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well positioned to capitalise on the momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing finance for the low-carbon transition; continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and sustainable organisation; and work with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Chief Executive Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The HKMA’s objective in its sustainability work is to lead by example through its own policies and operations, ensure that both Hong Kong’s financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to the risks of climate change, and support the transition to more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also contribute to the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the sector’s climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management practices and a new round of consultation meetings as part of the assessment of banks’ progress in implementing supervisory requirements for climate risk management; continuing work to incorporate climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; completing the second round of the sector-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to align applicable requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s Pillar 3¹ framework for climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance with the industry on best practices for transition planning. To promote the sound development of banks’ provision of green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain dialogue with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales processes. In addition, the HKMA will act as a facilitator by promoting the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon publish a local green taxonomy and continue to broaden its coverage to include more activities, such as transition activities. Meanwhile, we will continue to explore the use of technological solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the forthcoming cloud-based platform designed to facilitate banks’ physical risk assessments. To enhance practitioners’ professional capabilities, we will also develop the professional level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking in 2024. Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposal in the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market, while attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates to raise green capital through Hong Kong and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme to expand Hong Kong’s green finance talent pool. As Co-Chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives that promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three areas: sustainability disclosures, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another priority, through the Green Commercial Banking Alliance, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing distinctive market insights and targeted professional training for banks, and offering practical guidance to help banks support financial institutions in developing tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also deepen our collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment, and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “investment portfolio” by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring portfolio resilience throughout the journey towards net zero. Recognising that the goals of the Paris Agreement can be achieved only through an economy-wide transition, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus, while taking into account the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives, on assets that can deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy. As an environmentally responsible organisation, the HKMA will continue to update its decarbonisation strategy to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA’s climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. We will also continue to actively encourage staff participation in our sustainability efforts, including by launching campaigns to foster sustainable habits and enhancing office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers’ ESG practices when selecting suppliers and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the prescribed certification standards. In the regular upgrading of data centre facilities, we will not only keep pace with the latest technological developments but also incorporate green designs and practices. Meanwhile, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in the social focus area, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion, improve financial literacy, and raise public awareness of precautions against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to reducing its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central bank, banking sector regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to guide the formulation of its sustainability strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of related initiatives, and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and practices. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability work; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides management-level leadership for the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies; in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and, for other functional areas, relevant committees and working groups that plan and implement sustainability initiatives relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s different functional areas1. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters in the four functional areas of the banking sector, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s functional departments; assesses the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees its external communications strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans concerning their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Development and Services Division, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the CASG2 in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the CASG provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable financial centre in Asia and globally. For details of the CASG’s work, see the chapter “Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong’s financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to the impacts of various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their important functions in the financial system and channel more capital into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to respond to and manage climate risk, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is committed to developing various policy measures to enhance the banking system’s capacity to address climate risk. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economy’s transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition-planning practices. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry and organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience within the industry. Regarding disclosure requirements, in light of the latest international developments, including the publication of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s consultation in November on a Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that is aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into banking supervisory processes. Climate risk management has now become a standing agenda item at prudential meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors also use the enhanced CAMEL rating system1, which has incorporated climate risk factors, to assess banks’ risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into banking supervisory processes, the HKMA revised its “Greenness” assessment framework to focus on banks’ transition-planning practices. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks for addressing climate risk. Key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023 Following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”, the HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews of climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covered four major areas: the governance framework for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategies, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organisational culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of enhancements to the climate risk stress-testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of concurrent economic and climate-change shocks. Following these enhancements and as part of the HKMA’s regular regulator-led stress-testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks’ climate risk exposures and further strengthen their capacity to manage climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of climate risk stress testing, an increase of more than 60% compared with the inaugural pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a Climate Risk Stress Testing Forum in November, attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experience among banks, the event helped deepen the industry’s overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks’ progress in implementing the HKMA’s Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”. The HKMA met with bank management to discuss their climate risk management efforts and common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided banks with targeted recommendations to encourage and support them in continuing to enhance their climate risk management capabilities in accordance with the HKMA’s supervisory expectations. As global attention to climate change and efforts to address it continue to grow, the HKMA has observed increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer demand. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks’ sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards that the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing good practices observed. The circular covers various areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and books and records, with the aim of mitigating potential greenwashing risks and enhancing investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, strengthening banks’ capacity to manage climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. The HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable approaches to combating money laundering through the application of advanced analytics and A.I., thereby reducing the use of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online common data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks’ operational processes for the sustainable submission of anti-money laundering-related data. In September, the HKMA organised the “Green Fintech Competition” to identify market-ready solutions that could help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability- or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised the “Green and Sustainable Banking Conference”, providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, while also announcing the results of the “Green Fintech Competition”. The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and promote greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green classification framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the “Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong” to solicit stakeholders’ views on the development and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is refining the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crime as a predicate offence for money laundering; given the interconnections between anti-money laundering and environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues, this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators. Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial vulnerability analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of risks to financial stability and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Plans Working Group, the HKMA participates in analysing the interactions between the transition plans of financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective for assessing climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impacts of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics included the climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on housing prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance across the global supply chain5. The findings of these studies enhanced the HKMA’s understanding of the implications of climate change and ESG issues for financial stability and supported the formulation of relevant policies. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related issues, the HKMA Research Memorandum series, and other channels. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In accordance with NGFS recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, while drawing on the insights gained to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, supporting international initiatives, and aligning with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a more vibrant ecosystem and further advance green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial sector’s response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government’s climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key initiatives to support Hong Kong in capitalising on sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work including sustainability disclosures, ecosystem development, transition finance and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainability Disclosures Working Group was established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong’s adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group was also established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on the data front, we continued to promote the adoption of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire for non-listed firms2, which the Steering Group launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong’s position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capitalise on the investment and finance opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support skills training in the industry, the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre under the Steering Group implemented the Government’s Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates undertaking green and sustainable finance-related training and acquiring relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible programmes or qualifications under the Scheme, and more than 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched the foundation level of a new Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. This module aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking sector to develop the professional level of the module to meet the industry’s rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, particularly SMEs, better understand key climate- and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and transition planning, the HKMA collaborated during the year with relevant government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners including CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3 and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)4, to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops that attracted participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative in 2022, training programmes were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns’ and university bachelor’s degree graduates’ understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology to bridge climate-related data gaps and improve data quality, the HKMA is committed to making relevant data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, corporates and the public with one-stop access to green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements included an electronic sustainability disclosure platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, easy-to-browse and searchable data and resources. During Hong Kong Green Week, the Steering Group also co-organised the “Climate Tech for Sustainable Finance” event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong’s strengths in green technology. The “Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Stream” was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia and consultancy firms. The flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week was the Climate Business Forum: Asia-Pacific, co-hosted by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together more than 400 guests, including leading decision-makers in global business and finance, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event explored a wide range of issues, including the energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industry, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in Asia-Pacific emerging and developing markets. The forum received strong support from public- and private-sector organisations, which co-organised more than 10 roundtables, seminars and other networking events. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, finance for the net-zero transition, green finance taxonomies, and green development finance in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the Asian Climate Finance Roundtable on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures for scaling up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events formed part of the HKMA’s broader efforts to foster and enrich Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms for participants to promote new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the Green Commercial Bank Alliance5 as a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking sector associations, research institutions and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting more than 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB published their second thought leadership report, entitled “Developing a High-Ambition Climate Strategy for Green Banking: A Case Study.” In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the thought leadership report “Developing a High-Ambition Climate Strategy for Green Banking: A Case Study.” During the year, the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI) and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, while channelling more capital into green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong Chapter to support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA supports GFANZ’s work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists with green bond issuance under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent in institutional and retail green bonds, with the proceeds allocated to more than 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. To enhance the Programme’s transparency and accountability, the Government publishes a Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023–24 financial year, the Government continued its regular institutional green bond issuances and issued approximately US$6 billion equivalent in green bonds in June. The triple-currency offering comprised bonds with different tenors denominated in US dollars, euros and RMB, attracting various categories of investors and receiving an enthusiastic response, with subscriptions totalling nearly US$30 billion equivalent. The issuance size of the RMB bonds increased from RMB10 billion in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year RMB bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government’s RMB yield curve and further diversify offshore renminbi product offerings. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds totalling HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and financial inclusion. The issuance provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them both to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As an important global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in support of the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading investment in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to exercise active ownership and integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of “Capital Preservation First, Long-Term Growth”1, the HKMA believes that giving due consideration to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a “net-zero emissions by 2050” target2 for its “investment portfolio”, the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, with an emphasis on sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better long-term risk-adjusted returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA contributes to building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial and central banking communities. Through stewardship and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA is committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development advance in tandem. Figure 1 The Exchange Fund’s responsible investment journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial to integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. To fulfil its commitments in support of the Glasgow Declaration3 of the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by preparing this chapter on the Exchange Fund’s responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives while practising responsible investment. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Exchange Fund Investment Office’s various ESG initiatives. Proposals discussed and work progress reviewed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across the HKMA’s different functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 Responsible investment governance structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office began its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy function led by the Chief Strategy Officer to coordinate and lead the Office’s strategic development, incorporating the Responsible Investment Team formerly under the Risk Management and Compliance Division—now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA’s shift in responsible investment from a risk-based focus to a more proactive and forward-looking approach to addressing investment-related sustainability issues. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams across the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors and assists its senior management in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across various investment programmes: Public market investments—The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into the credit risk panel data model with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed-income portfolios through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see “Promoting Active Ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 40 for details). Private market investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4 arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, can affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The United Nations Environment Programme’s Emissions Gap Report 20235 projects that, unless further reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are made worldwide, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5°C to 2.9°C above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more ambitious policies, technological development or behavioural changes to curb temperature increases may intensify transition risks, such as shocks from asset depreciation or stranded assets. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is consistent with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund’s “investment portfolio” to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections describe this approach in detail. Figure 3 The HKMA’s three-pronged approach to responsible investment On the path towards its net-zero target, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusions or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in corporates undergoing transition that possess outstanding technologies and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including corporates in high-emitting industries. Second, tackling climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from the relevant investments does not resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership to support these industries, the HKMA encourages them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby bringing about positive change both within the industries themselves and globally. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy, adopting a holistic approach to pursue transition outcomes aligned with the net-zero objectives of both the Exchange Fund and the world, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate the climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s asset portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA’s responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and extended the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another externally managed asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA outperformed their investment benchmark, demonstrating the concept of “doing well by doing good”. In private markets, the HKMA actively builds a resilient, long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as the climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, demonstrating its commitment to addressing Asia’s climate-transition needs. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems, which rely on energy-intensive, high-temperature environments to produce plastics, the company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. Made entirely from waste, this plastic material can replace petroleum-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables, providing a sustainable and versatile alternative. It is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a staunch supporter of the circular economy. The HKMA committed two tranches of USD1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the International Finance Corporation in 2021 to create MCPP One Planet, a new global climate-related investment platform and the world’s first Paris Agreement-aligned cross-sectoral emerging-market loan portfolio. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The International Finance Corporation collected data on MCPP loans. According to its report, the HKMA’s loan commitments have supported emerging markets and developing countries in areas including economic transition and human capital development. Specifically, projects financed by the HKMA are projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gas emissions from a typical petrol-powered passenger vehicle travelling 14 billion miles. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organization and is taking a multipronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA attaches importance to employee well-being and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible organization, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under the three pillars of the environment, employees and social responsibility. Established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee)1 is the principal decision-making body for organizational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee’s predecessor was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating its vision, strategies and policies on organizational sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Working Group and the Volunteer Services Group support the coordination of organizational sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and discussing ways to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition. The focus is on implementing carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly operating practices, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to use carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while using carbon offsets for emissions that are difficult to abate. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operating solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate with the HKMA to electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool and places emphasis on employee well-being. In respect of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers engaging social enterprises in procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and works with the banking sector to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all sectors of society.
