The remainder of this chapter sets out details of the above strategies. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee,2 chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more frequent extreme weather, may affect the HKMA’s offices and impede employee travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. Various measures have also been incorporated into office design to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA’s energy use, air travel and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption and paper consumption. The HKMA’s climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 (air travel) greenhouse gas emissions across all areas of its organizational operations by 2050 or earlier. As its near-term emission reduction targets, the HKMA plans to eliminate Scope 1 emissions entirely by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles, and to reduce Scope 2 emissions intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier, against a 2015 baseline, through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multipronged approach, as far as practicable, to minimize Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, such as those associated with paper consumption, waste generation and air travel. The HKMA’s long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which was also validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper consumption and waste data disclosed in this report.6 The scope and criteria of the verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, the HKMA issued a standalone 2022 Sustainability Report for the first time. The HKMA’s efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognized with an ESG Award in the Public Sector/Not-for-Profit category of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants’ Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023. The HKMA was the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for achieving a high standard of ESG performance, producing a clear and readable Sustainability Report, and demonstrating its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting by appointing an independent organization to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report. In addition, the HKMA received the top-ranking Gold Award in the “Non-profit Making and Charitable Organizations” category of the Hong Kong Management Association’s 2023 Best Annual Reports Awards. The judging panel commended the HKMA’s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making effective use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA’s commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts of its operations, and its internal Green Office Guidelines provide employees with guidance on resource use and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, repair and maintenance of the offices it owns and leases. When refurbishing offices, existing furniture and fit-out materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decorative materials are given priority. The HKMA’s continued adoption of this approach resulted in parts of its offices at Two International Finance Centre that were refurbished in 2021 and 2022 receiving LEED7 Gold certification and BEAM Plus Interiors8 Gold certification, respectively. Enhancing energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and effective use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA’s key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good practices, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to conserve electricity, other energy-saving measures include using light-emitting diode lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA’s energy consumption continued to decrease, reaching 2.59 MWh9 per capita in 2023, down 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA’s daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly arise from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e10 per capita, down 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardizing equipment, office software and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, built a digital working environment, and strengthened online collaboration within the organization.11 Paperless meetings have become the HKMA’s primary mode of conducting meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, internal administrative matters are handled primarily through electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages employees to embrace green and digital working practices by replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, implementation of an electronic record-keeping system is also under way. The above green and digital initiatives have delivered positive results. The HKMA’s paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per capita, representing a substantial decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events returned to in-person formats following the COVID-19 pandemic, and given the need to promote Hong Kong’s development as an international financial centre, overseas business travel by relevant HKMA employees was unavoidable. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees attending overseas events to take direct flights or combine different business trips where practicable. At the organizational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participated in Gold Standard12-certified carbon offsetting programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes involve waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA’s procurement process takes sustainability and environmental considerations into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organization’s procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalized and aligned with the environmental specifications in the Government’s Green Procurement List, particularly for the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have also been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. Meanwhile, all suppliers are required to undertake to comply with environmental regulations. In accordance with the “4R” principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle—the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimizing waste generation and managing waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to support the development of targeted waste management strategies. A breakdown of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, is provided in the “Performance Summary” section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated directly for the first time in the red packet recycling programme organized by the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Employees contributed approximately 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the following Lunar New Year. As the HKMA’s operational and backup data centres account for a major share of the organization’s overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres and achieve optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE).13 In 2023, the HKMA’s two data centres received Gold and Platinum ratings, respectively, under the BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organization in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has long been a key focus of the technical team. To this end, the team adopted green designs in refurbishment works and implemented good energy-efficiency practices to lower PUE and meet the relevant targets, including round-the-clock monitoring of the data centres’ environmental facilities and continuous enhancement of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to improve energy use at the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review comprehensively assessing the data centres’ green performance and developing recommendations for further improvements in all areas. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the study was completed, the HKMA also began preparing to obtain Green Data Centre certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process was highly comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented enhancement measures based on the consultant’s recommendations, improving areas ranging from energy performance to health-related aspects of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2023 environmental data (“2023 Data”). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and changes in these data compared with 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level recorded when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data was prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparisons (except for food waste). The scope of verification covered a total of five office and warehouse assets, comprising four offices located at (1) Two International Finance Centre, (2) Hopewell Centre, (3) One Pacific Place, and (4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at (5) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the five assets. This verification was performed in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion with a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and also reviewed and tested the reliability of the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for collecting and reporting the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2023 Data and concludes that the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable, and that the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first year in which the global temperature exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached a new high, highlighting the inadequacy of current climate change mitigation measures. As efforts to combat global warming continue, climate-related risks are bound to become more pronounced, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. In addition, current geopolitical tensions, the increasing fragmentation of the global economy, the potential worsening of energy security concerns, and an uncertain economic outlook are all creating greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained funding support. Among regions worldwide, Asia faces particularly acute transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has noted, Asia is not only an engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the effects of climate change. Asia therefore plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve its net-zero emissions target. As Asia’s leading international financial centre, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the region’s transition. To this end, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively embedding sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses both on strengthening the financial sector’s ability to address climate change-related risks and on helping the sector seize the emerging opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector in its transition to net zero, investing in a sustainable future, financing net zero, and fostering more inclusive sustainability. The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong’s and Asia’s net-zero transition, but banks themselves also face considerable risks during the transition process. Under the Action Agenda, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance their disclosure of climate change-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks’ climate risk management, we also provide guidance on transition planning to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage the associated risks. We are also carrying out preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong’s sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing industry transparency in related activities. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year by incorporating more sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we aim to direct more capital towards sustainability- and transition-related projects. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. At the same time, however, it also presents the Exchange Fund with opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience has shown that investment returns and positive sustainability impacts can be mutually compatible and are not inherently in conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier, and under the Action Agenda have pledged to support Asia’s climate transition through the Exchange Fund’s investments. Sustainable investments currently account for more than 10% of the Investment Portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate Asia’s transition to a low-carbon economy through co-investment. In addition, we published the inaugural “HKMA ESG Expectations” document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. The mobilisation of capital is particularly important for accelerating the region’s transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond offerings by Asian issuers, including provincial and municipal governments in the Mainland, Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling capital to accelerate the region’s transition. The Action Agenda outlines a vision for developing Hong Kong into the region’s preferred sustainable finance platform, as well as the objective of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Sustainable Bond Programme to promote green bond innovation—including the issuance of the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year—to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme in May last year to cover transition finance instruments, and launching the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have remained committed to encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise the capital required for their decarbonisation transition. A robust transition requires not only capital and innovation, but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosures, and industry professionals equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, under the Action Agenda we have pledged to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures and to help bridge the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge across the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing convenient and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosures by small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the professional-level “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners to strengthen the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged people from different sectors in sustainability discussions, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainability vision. Under the Action Agenda, we have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions from our own operations by 2030 or earlier, bringing forward our original commitment by 20 years. In addition, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the Government. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve operational efficiency through digitalisation, cultivate a culture of sustainability within the organisation, and encourage staff to participate actively in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has always been a cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in geopolitics have introduced further uncertainty into global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an indisputable reality and is progressively intensifying. The current situation leaves no room for complacency in our efforts to address climate change. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong’s financial system while creating opportunities along the way. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, work tirelessly to advance sustainability, and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges, we will remain steadfast in supporting the development of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the present generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future directions, the timelines for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant initiatives. Through strategic policy development, enhanced regulatory engagement and improvements to internal operations, the HKMA plans to strengthen the capacity of Hong Kong’s financial sector and the HKMA itself to address climate change risks, while promoting Asia’s transition towards a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exert influence and contribute to the development of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in remaining safe and sound throughout the transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - conducting a new round of thematic reviews and a third round of consultation meetings on banks’ climate risk management practices to assess their implementation of the HKMA’s relevant regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - completing work to incorporate climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s regulator-led stress-testing framework; - continuing to advance the incorporation of climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; - commencing preparations to formulate relevant regulatory requirements for the local banking sector’s implementation of the climate-related financial risk Pillar 3 disclosure framework to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - completing the preparation of a new module, GS-2, of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide banks with guidance on transition planning; and - sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking sector regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool for identifying green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating the flow of related capital. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the taxonomy to broaden its coverage, including the incorporation of transition elements, the addition of green economic activities and the inclusion of climate change adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will hold another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks’ adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the region’s sustainable financing needs. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, whose expanded scope will cover sustainable projects such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and provide a demonstration effect for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide grants under the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, encouraging more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise sustainable capital. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates from the Mainland and other regions to raise green capital in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing grants under the Digital Bond Grant Scheme to prospective issuers of digital green bonds. Despite growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and corporates, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with a wider range of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be used to make existing resources more accessible and convenient; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training required by the industry. The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, creating a need to expand the local talent pool and bridge knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA’s key priorities for 2025 include working with the banking sector to develop professional-level training programmes for the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners, and identifying areas in which the industry requires further training through the forthcoming Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030 study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to step up promotion of the government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme and review the scope of the scheme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market insights, delivering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop road maps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in support of the broader economic transition. Through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, we will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can contribute to positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in corporate sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving its net-zero commitment announced in the Action Agenda, the HKMA will continue to advance corporate sustainability by progressively incorporating environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessments and reporting at a pragmatic pace. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technological solutions to assess the material impact of climate risk on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government’s publication of the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to applying the principles of energy efficiency and conservation when selecting a data centre for the planned upgrade project. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, while improving the overall digital experience of our staff, banks and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking sector regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and working practices. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability efforts. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level for the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies; - in responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Office; and - in other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups responsible for planning and implementing sustainability initiatives relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s various functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans concerning ESG-related matters in four functional areas: the banking sector, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; - oversee the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s various functional departments; - assess the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - oversee external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development matters are also invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major outcomes and future plans relating to their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable financial centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group’s work, see the chapter “Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem.”

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen the Hong Kong financial system’s capacity to address climate risk while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are affected by various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risk. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by directing capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risk and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA announced the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (the “Action Agenda”), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading sustainable financial centre in the region and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Agenda comprises eight goals under four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant banking policy goals, we have been undertaking the work described below. All banks strive to achieve net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks enhance transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2, “Transition Planning.” The new module is intended to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and manage the associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to incorporating into the assessment process relevant factors set out by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risk. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Agenda. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help direct capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors and is intended to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy and the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating elements relevant to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the Taxonomy’s coverage and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into banking supervisory processes. To help banks enhance their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking sector good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, mainly including: - establishing a robust governance framework that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board and senior management; - ensuring effective oversight of key areas relating to climate-related risks: (1) facilitating and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable focusing on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management.” The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA conducted a second series of consultation meetings to assess a new group of banks’ progress in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management,” and understand the challenges they faced. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to the specific circumstances of individual banks to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that, under various scenarios, including one assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risk and a macroeconomic downturn, the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risk. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the exercise was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognises the numerous data- and methodology-related challenges banks face in climate risk management and has therefore been pursuing a range of initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Going forward, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published a practical application guide and two Regtech Use Case Briefs (English versions) describing technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third FiNETech event, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore collaboration in green fintech. Recognising that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial vulnerability analyses and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of risks to financial stability and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA contributed to the further development of climate scenarios to help central banks and regulators understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Working Group on Transition Plans, the HKMA participated in analysing the interactions between the transition plans of financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Green Technology Application in Banking: A Practice Guide” (English version), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technologies to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects to examine the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in cushioning monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition towards a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, supporting the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helps strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandum series. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission corporates can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission corporates. The study was featured in the HKIMR’s Insights from Monetary Research and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this participation, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, while drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by advancing financing for net zero and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to establishing Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable finance platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial market, enhancing sustainability disclosures across the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Establish Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable finance platform in the region and globally Catalyse sustainable finance innovation Support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures Bridge talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government’s determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to more than 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including their currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a green and sustainable finance hub, its scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (“Sustainable Bond Programme”). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes a Green Bond Report annually, detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency offering comprised bonds of various tenors denominated in RMB, US dollars and euros. The bonds attracted participation from a diverse range of investors and received an enthusiastic response, with subscriptions exceeding US$15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20- and 30-year RMB green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and were its longest-tenor RMB bonds to date, providing new market benchmarks and further demonstrating the role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further broadened the range of offshore renminbi investment products available in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bonds reflected investors’ recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s finance platform to raise capital for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, launched in May 2021, which provides grants for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As at the end of 2024, grants had been approved under the Scheme for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with an aggregate value exceeding US$140 billion. In May 2024, the Scheme was extended for three years to 2027, and its scope was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong’s transition finance platform to progressively decarbonise. - Grants approved for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with an aggregate value exceeding US$140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope expanded to cover transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable finance platform, achieving encouraging results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, including RMB2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds and RMB900 million of social bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion of blue bonds and RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds. These bond issuances once again highlighted Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable fund flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. With the above measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as Asia’s preferred sustainable finance platform. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained Asia’s largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in 2024. Bonds arranged in Hong Kong totalled US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, respectively the world’s first tokenised government green bond and the world’s first multi-currency digital bond. These issuances demonstrated the Government’s support for market participants in the region in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bond issuances, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (“Steering Group”) has been working towards the adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (“ISSB Standards”) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (“Questionnaire”), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by corporates, including small and medium-sized enterprises (“SMEs”). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024, enabling corporates to complete it online (see the QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire in light of industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including identifying the Questionnaire’s core questions and providing common use cases. In addition, we are seeking to improve the Questionnaire’s compatibility with other supporting tools on the Steering Group’s website. For more information about the Questionnaire, please visit the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, demonstrating its commitment. The Report contains extensive information, including the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks and its plans and implementation progress for achieving climate targets. For details of sustainability disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA”. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking sector and facilitating knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local banking practitioners’ knowledge and skills in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (“HKIB”) launched the foundation level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in July 2023. The module is designed to help banking professionals acquire knowledge of green and sustainable finance and develop relevant professional competencies more effectively. It covers four key areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance and governance. In addition, the professional level of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, aimed at middle- and senior-level banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was launched in November. To provide banking practitioners with the necessary training, the HKIB, as the administrator of the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module, launched a foundation-level training programme for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking sector in 2025 to develop a professional-level training programme. To understand the banking sector’s further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently working with the sector on the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030” study, with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it formulate and adjust talent development strategies and initiatives to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to support the implementation of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students undertaking training related to sustainable finance. As at December 2024, 85 international and local programmes had been registered as eligible training programmes under the Scheme, and more than 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (“CASI”), the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focusing on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (“GFANZ”) in establishing a Hong Kong chapter in October and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritises sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of “capital preservation first, long-term growth thereafter,” believing that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate the associated investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment practices. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better long-term returns corrected for risk. We incorporate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital towards sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA issued the “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial sector and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development progress in tandem. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while taking into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Exchange Fund Investment Office’s ESG initiatives. Proposals and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across the HKMA’s different functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on incorporating ESG factors and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across different types of investments: - Public market investments—The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the incorporation of ESG factors into the credit risk panel data model with reference to input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (for details, see “Promoting Active Ownership” under the “Risk Management” section on page 39). - Private market investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks and related opportunities arising from climate change may affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2024 published by the United Nations Environment Programme estimates that the global average temperature will rise by 2.6°C to 3.1°C above pre-industrial levels unless there is rapid, large-scale global mobilisation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Uncertainty surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, resulting in greater market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also expose investments to additional risks of physical damage and financial loss. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities with potentially attractive long-term prospects in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related considerations when incorporating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this target (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the “Action Agenda,” which reinforced the Exchange Fund’s commitments and efforts relating to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement rather than exclusion or divestment from the investible universe. Investing in a Sustainable Future Achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier - Actively broaden the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly climate-transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Incorporate ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition outlook considerations - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply with them - Commit to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio by 67% from its 2017 level by 2030 or earlier Supporting the Region’s Transition Through Investment - Continue to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continue to identify and prioritise high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia’s transition and generate positive impacts globally First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investible universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in corporates that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technologies and sound corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including corporates in high-emitting industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Simply excluding or divesting from relevant investments does not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership, encouraging them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon operating practices and thereby bringing about positive changes for both the industries themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, thereby driving comprehensive decarbonisation across the economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of a portfolio depends not only on correction within the portfolio itself, but also on broad-based economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategy in 2024 by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero objectives of both the Exchange Fund and the world. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including the incorporation of ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting various types of assets aligned with pathways towards net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or corporates providing climate solutions, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on investments that facilitate transition. By incorporating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolios. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio,” with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments—The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the use of a customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the relevant case studies in “Enhancing Sustainability Through GSS Bonds”). - Private market investments—The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio and capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and assesses investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see examples in “Joining Forces to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond”). - Passive portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios whose investment benchmarks are not ESG indices - Actively managed governance-themed portfolios - Actively managed ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonisation globally, in Asia and across the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The “MCPP One Planet” programme, providing Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental institution. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects encompass enhancements to monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling. In addition to the continuous treatment of wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving sludge recycling rates of up to 100%. The facilities also use gases generated during sludge treatment to fuel boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond finances multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a country’s canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river water to arid regions. The project’s primary objective is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining to prevent leakage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA’s key priorities in delivering on this commitment in 2024 was its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than originally planned and in line with the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda”. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to supporting staff training and well-being, advancing financial inclusion, and enhancing the public’s financial literacy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee) is the principal decision-making body for corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030 as part of the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) provides guidance on implementing sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. An additional layer of support is provided by the Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Services Team, which comprise staff from different operational departments; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ways to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteering activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and the community as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around the three pillars of environmental, staff and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonising and digitalising the HKMA’s daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with Government guidelines - Promote greener operating practices across the financial sector and the wider community - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens staff’s sense of belonging - Provide a high-quality work environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Foster a culture of caring for the community - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance the public’s financial literacy through consumer education initiatives The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced a plan to bring forward its target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than its original commitment, as part of the “Action Agenda”. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition to net zero, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations by reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the power generation fuel mix of local electricity companies. In addition, the HKMA has established a digital workplace to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. The HKMA also recognises the importance of fostering a sustainability culture and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainability-supporting practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under its overarching 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procure low-carbon products and services wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023 the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offset programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market’s low-carbon transition through measures ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to the promotion of electronic payments and the collection of coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA’s strategies for leading environmental protection efforts, promoting staff well-being and caring for the community.
