Under the HKMA’s overall corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To assess more effectively the potential operational impacts of climate change, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring operational continuity, the HKMA’s offices incorporate a range of measures into their design to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup-facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions and waste generated by its own operations, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated using fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods, including capital goods, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to this report. The HKMA leads by example by adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 with a view to achieving fully green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, repair and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects carried out in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fit-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres. In a data centre facility upgrade project in 2024, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices in line with manufacturers’ software update cycles, thereby extending the period during which the devices can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to support the development of targeted waste-management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are located at convenient points throughout the HKMA’s offices. To increase the recycling rate, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Pledge for Events”, committing to measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that comply with the environmental specifications in the Government’s “Green Procurement List”, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as by combining multiple trips wherever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard-certified carbon offset programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes focus on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. Beginning on Earth Day, 22 April 2024, and continuing throughout May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. This provided a valuable opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment and drive to embed environmental sustainability in its internal operations. Activities included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Planet” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “kokedama” indoor plants originating from Japan. Waste-audit results were also shared, and an operator of a community recycling centre introduced recycling best practices. To sustain the momentum of “Green Month”, the HKMA launched an approximately six-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that the cumulative effect of small changes in individual habits could significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the “Green Actions Made Easy” video, in which several senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders, encouraging staff to lead by example in reducing waste and increasing recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to assess employees’ understanding of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green-office measures. The survey results will support the future development of sustainability training activities and waste-management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA regards itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to leading and accelerating the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable operating practices across the financial sector and the community as a whole. The HKMA has introduced a range of measures to improve the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform’s coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, facilitating their submission of certain regulatory information. The expanded coverage is intended to further streamline submission processes for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 included SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a simplified submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a central platform providing users with advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verified the environmental data (“Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, and their respective intensities for 2024. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, together with their corresponding intensities, for 2023 and 2024. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covered a total of six office and warehouse assets, comprising five offices located at: 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the six assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the Data were tested by tracing selected sample data to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking were also reviewed and subjected to reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for collecting and reporting the Data. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency’s verification team was not involved in the Data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - the Data are materially accurate and reliable; and - the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu Yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
